California, New York, and Florida represent the top state exposures for this business model.

best_narrative.headline: Zocdoc: Telehealth Rivals File Federal Lobbying on Prescription Economics
best_narrative.body: Zocdoc operates a healthcare directory and appointment platform with embedded telehealth marketplace functionality, creating direct exposure to prescribing economics regulation and state medical advertising oversight distinct from pure-play telehealth operators. Four competitors recently filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth policy topics, signaling coordinated industry mobilization around prescription access and reimbursement frameworks. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for this business model include anti-kickback statute compliance, state medical board advertising restrictions, and consumer protection rules governing telehealth referral economics. NY, CA, and TX represent material exposure given top-3 state status and these states' active enforcement on telehealth fee arrangements.
best_narrative.cold_first_touch_frame:
Subject: Competitor Telehealth Lobbying Filings Suggest NY Policy Shift Ahead Dear Public Policy Head, Four telehealth competitors filed federal lobbying disclosures in May on prescription economics and access topics. This typically precedes state-level rulemaking on fee-splitting and referral economics. Your government affairs team should model how NY's medical board might tighten telehealth advertising or prescribing-incentive rules within the next 12 months. Would a 15-minute call Thursday work to discuss early-stage state intelligence on this trend? Best,
[Rep Name]
best_narrative.worked_deal_revival_frame: BDR: We've seen four telehealth competitors mobilize federally on prescription economics in the last month. This usually signals state regulators are preparing guidance on telehealth fee arrangements, and NY is typically first to act. Prospect: We haven't tracked this angle yet, and our GA team is focused on provider licensing right now. BDR Pivot: That makes sense. A 10-minute sync with your compliance leadership on what NY's medical board is signaling would help you get ahead before enforcement notices drop. Do you have 10 minutes next Wednesday?

best_narrative.headline: Spring Health: Competitor Telehealth Lobbying Intensifies NY Behavioral Health Licensing

Competitors have filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth topics as recently as April 2026, signaling active policy mobilization around prescribing standards and licensure portability. Operators in this segment commonly face material exposure in top-three states like New York around asynchronous behavioral health delivery and practitioner credential reciprocity. Government affairs teams should monitor competitor filings and state licensing board activity to anticipate advocacy positioning that could shift reimbursement or prescribing frameworks.
